content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp, cake or patty (1363) is a ready‑to‑eat seafood product formed into small patties. The shrimp is peeled, minced, mixed with breadcrumbs, spices and sometimes egg, then shaped into a patty and cooked by steaming, frying or baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp is one of the fastest‑growing seafood species and can be farmed in aquaculture.
Shrimp patties are popular in Asian cuisines, especially in Japan (tempura) and Thailand (krato).
Shrimp provides more protein per weight than most fish varieties.
Shrimp gets its pink hue from astaxanthin, a powerful antioxidant.
Patty‑style shrimp cakes are convenient for storage and microwave reheating.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Shrimp contains about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many meat patties, shrimp patties have low saturated fat content.

items.title: Provides iodine and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are essential for thyroid function and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Contains astaxanthin
items.content: Astaxanthin offers strong antioxidant benefits for eye and skin health.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Low cholesterol and the presence of omega‑3 fatty acids favor cardiovascular health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contains moderate cholesterol; people with hypercholesterolemia should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared patties often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some manufacturers add preservatives and flavor enhancers that may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Shrimp patties can be enjoyed hot or cold, added to salads, soups, burgers, or served with tartar sauce, soy sauce, or lemon juice. They reheat well on a skillet, in the oven, or in a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product refrigerated at 0–4 °C in its original packaging and consume within 3 days after opening. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 2 months. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.
